_comments: The BizApps Contracts Application — what makes this app appear in MJ Explorer at all.
WITHOUT THIS FILE the app is invisible. CodeGen auto-creates a schema-named application
(__mj_BizAppsContracts) that carries the entities, but that is a container for admin access,
not a destination: it has no nav items and no icon, so nobody finds the app by looking.
This row is the user-facing app.
DefaultNavItems IS the top nav bar. Each item is ResourceType 'Custom' pointing at a
DriverClass registered via @RegisterClass(BaseResourceComponent, '<DriverClass>') in
@mj-biz-apps/contracts-ng. BOTH HALVES ARE REQUIRED: metadata without a registered class
renders a dead tab, and a registered class without metadata never appears.
THREE ITEMS, organised by JOB rather than by entity (2026-08-05). Contracts is the agreement;
Billing is the money it produces; Setup is the configuration every contract inherits. Billing is
a PEER rather than a page beneath Contracts because 'what failed and why' is a different job,
done by different people at different times, from 'what did we agree' — filing one under the
other makes the smaller one invisible. Orders split Receivables out of Orders for the same
reason.
This file previously carried ONE item, with a comment arguing that everything in the app was one
section and movement belonged on a left rail. That was right about the rail and wrong about the
count, and the mistake was compounded by drawing a section switcher inside the page header with
mj-tab-nav — which LOOKS like a top nav bar and is not one. A strip drawn in a page gets no deep
links, no resource state and no place in the app switcher. MJ's rule is top nav ACROSS sections
and left nav WITHIN one; honouring the first half means real nav items, not a picture of them.
DefaultForNewUser is true so the app lands for new users without a per-persona grant. When
it is false you must run `mjdev apps enable <slug> <app>` or the app stays hidden even though
everything is installed correctly — a confusing failure that looks like a build problem.
The fixed UUID means a re-push against a rebuilt database UPDATES this row rather than
creating a second Application with the same name.

fields.Name: Contracts
fields.Description: The agreement envelope — commitment, term structure, escalation, renewal and the billing event. Contracts decides what is owed and when; orders remains the only place anyone is billed.
